meta.storyTitle: Make the tracker push, sync and post stages handle an ISSUE-anchored work item

alternativesConsidered.name: Kind-aware head end to end (context + persistence + chain + adoption + linkage)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One definitionHeadJsonPath/requireApprovedDefinition rule at all five layers; integration tests per finding; DEF byte-identical.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Carry the DEF-then-ISSUE head kind end to end through all five layers with one head-path helper. gates.ts gains requireApprovedDefinition (approved-gated, { kind, artifact, jsonPath }) and definitionHeadJsonPath (DEF json if existsSync else ISSUE json — the storage.ts readEpicDefinitionCore order). Layers: (1) context assemblers branch on kind (DEF byte-identical; ISSUE via impliedIssueStories + issue title + new renderIssueEpicBody); (2) persistence: mutateEpicTrackerMeta (orchestrator.ts:2972) and sync.ts (:59, :106, :164) use definitionHeadJsonPath/impliedIssueStories so meta.tracker lands on ISSUE-<hash>.json with zero DEF fabricated; (3) chain computeNextAction ISSUE branch (chain.ts:325-360) falls through to the DEF tracker steps after the story loop; (4) adoption: push seeds PushContext.existingRefs.epicRef + storyRefs[s1] from ISSUE.meta.tracker.issueRef and finalize binds EPIC-<hash> + STORY-<hash>-s1 heads to it via bindUnitIssue (idempotent same-ref, conflict different-ref) — retries create 0 new remote issues; (5) linkDocsToIssues takes headKind, placement from workItemKindOf + anchor from requireEpicAnchor, ISSUE heads relink ISSUE.md + standalone s1 LLD.md and skip HLD/Define, never create docs/epics. Tests per layer incl. finalize on ISSUE-only fixture (readdir zero DEF), four-state chain sequence, adoption create-count 0 + conflict, linkage no-duplicate-folder.
pros: Closes all four review findings in one coherent change.
Reuses patchTrackerMeta (path-agnostic), bindArtifact (idempotent/conflict), PushContext.existingRefs adopt semantics, impliedIssueStories, workItemKindOf, issueArtifactPaths.
cons: Touches shared finalize/sync/link paths — mitigated by DEF parity tests (existing tests unedited pass).
Adoption identity (root issue = s1 story issue) must be stated explicitly.

alternativesConsidered.name: Persistence + chain only
alternativesConsidered.approach: Fix only persistence + chain (findings 1-2); defer adoption + linkage to a follow-up.
cons: Leaves HIGH finding 3 (duplicate remote issue via invisible issueRef) and MED finding 4 (docs/epics duplicate) open — the review blocks on all four.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Leaves HIGH finding 3 (duplicate remote issue via invisible issueRef) and MED finding 4 (docs/epics duplicate) open — the review blocks on all four

alternativesConsidered.name: Backfill bindings at approval
alternativesConsidered.approach: Backfill EPIC/STORY bindings at ISSUE approval time so unitIssueOf-based readers see the issue without per-layer kind branches, plus the linkDocsToIssues placement fix.
cons: Mutates the approval path (out of scope); changes when bindings appear; still needs the chain branch and persistence head-path fix; risks double-binding against bugfix/tracker.ts recordRefToDisk.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Mutates the approval path (out of scope), still needs the chain branch and persistence head-path fix, and risks double-binding against bugfix/tracker.ts recordRefToDisk

alternativesConsidered.name: Declare tracker stages DEF-only for bugs
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Chain-complete after LLD for ISSUE heads.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep generic tracker stages DEF-only for bugs: chain stays chain-complete after LLD for ISSUE heads; bugs use only bugfix/tracker.ts create/close.
cons: Is exactly the bug the ISSUE and finding 2 describe (unpushed ISSUE reports chain-complete).

postconditions: If ISSUE.meta.tracker.issueRef (readTrackerMeta) is set: seed existingRefs.epicRef + storyRefs[IMPLIED_ISSUE_STORY_ID]; ISSUE prompt adopts WITHOUT --force, labels added idempotently via singular --add-label (2.6a); finalize binds EPIC-<hash> + STORY-<hash>-s1 heads via bindUnitIssue (idempotent same-ref, conflict refuses); 0 new remote issues
If absent: the push path uses an ATOMIC CREATE-IF-ABSENT CLAIM, not a plain intent write

CLAIM (HIGH fix): BEFORE dispatching the mutating execute step, claimCreateIntent(repoPath, epicHash, runId) does writeFileSync(path, payload, { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 }) on .insrc/artifacts/PENDING-CREATE-<epicHash>.json (the same exclusive-create primitive the daemon uses for run files, src/daemon/run-file-ownership.ts:101 / managed-update-preparation.ts:46 — writeAtomic's tmp+rename would overwrite, 'wx' fails with EEXIST). Payload: { epicHash, runId (owner), owner, repo, title: issue.body.title, marker: '<!-- insrc:artifact ISSUE-<epicHash> -->', state: 'pending', createdAt, heartbeatAt }. On EEXIST the run reads the existing claim: if the owner's heartbeat is fresh (still executing) and state is 'pending'/'created', this run REFUSES to dispatch a create and instead adopts/reconciles per the claim; if the claim is abandoned (stale heartbeat, no persisted issueRef/head bindings), it may be displaced only by an ownership-verified replace.

RECONCILIATION RULE (ownership-safe): unresolved 'pending' claim (abandoned, or after a lost execute response) -> no create; candidates by persisted title via ghListIssuesByTitleTokenStrict (registry-table.ts:331), each body-verified by verifyRecoveryCandidate (2.6c: exact ISSUE-<hash> marker + owner/repo target); exactly one verified candidate -> adopt (update claim to 'created' under ownership check, persist issueRef + head bindings), 0 creates; zero or >1 verified -> explicit refusal naming the claim, human resolves. 'created' claims adopt their durable refs with 0 creates.

ALL claim ops (create, heartbeat, pending->created, takeover, delete) run inside the claim mutex and carry the fencing token; a displaced owner is rejected with ClaimOwnershipError and fenced from ALL subsequent persistence (issueRef write-back, head bindings, claim delete), closing the check-then-write race

api.name: claimCreateIntent + withClaimLock (mutex + fencing token on every claim op)
api.signature: function claimCreateIntent(repoPath: string, epicHash: string, runId: string): { claimed: true } | { claimed: false; existing }  // create-if-absent under the claim mutex; ALL claim ops go through withClaimLock(repoPath, epicHash, runId, expectedFence, op)

parameters.name: epicHash
parameters.purpose: Work-item hash; claim file name and mutex key

returns.meaning: claimed:true only when the 'wx' create succeeded while holding the claim mutex

errors.condition: any update/delete/takeover whose expectedFence does not equal the current claim's fence token — the op is rejected and the caller is fenced
claim file exists at create time
acquisition hits EEXIST against a live guard owner — fail closed with the conflict evidence, never reclaim a live holder

preconditions: called BEFORE the tracker.push execute step is dispatched; all later claim ops hold the same mutex
postconditions: Exactly one run holds the claim at a time: the claim file is created under the claim mutex with flag 'wx' (EEXIST -> claimed:false).

MUTEX LIFECYCLE (MED fix): the lock is a DIRECTORY guard, not a bare lock file — acquireRunFileGuard (src/shared/daemon-run-files.ts) pattern: mkdirSync(path, 0o700) + owner.json written with flag 'wx' inside, carrying ProcessIdentity { pid, startedAt, commandLine } + nonce. RELEASE: the holder removes its own guard on exit (recursive rm of its own pinned directory only, assertOwned first). CRASH RECOVERY: a newcomer that gets EEXIST runs quarantineDeadGuard (daemon-run-files.ts:269) — if owner.json's recorded pid is conclusively dead (pid liveness probe), the dead guard is quarantined (renamed aside under a reclaim claim) and re-acquired; a LIVE holder is never touched (the verdict withholds and the newcomer waits/fails closed with the conflict evidence). This is exactly the daemon guard's ownership/reclamation logic, not just O_EXCL.
So a crashed mutex holder never permanently blocks claim recovery; a fresh push reaches reconciliation after the crash, and a live holder is never broken.

FENCE token as before: every claim op under the mutex requires expectedFence === current and writes fence+1 in the same critical section; displaced owners are fenced from all later persistence with ClaimOwnershipError before any write.
TAKEOVER only for abandoned claims (stale heartbeat AND no persisted issueRef/head bindings), inside the mutex.

api.name: claimQueueKey (claim mutex mapped onto the artifact write-authority queue) + lock ordering
api.signature: const claimQueueKey = ArtifactIds.make({ kind: 'ISSUE', epicHash })  // 'ISSUE-<hash>' is a valid artifact id (SHAPES, artifact-ids.ts:70-95), so FileArtifactStore.exclusive / the daemon authority handler accept it; the on-disk claim file stays .insrc/artifacts/PENDING-CREATE-<epicHash>.json

parameters.name: epicHash
parameters.purpose: ISSUE-<hash> IS a valid queue key; PENDING-CREATE-<hash> is not (ArtifactIds.parse rejects unknown kinds) — the claim mutex uses the former, the claim file the latter

returns.meaning: the authority-accepted key for the claim's critical section

preconditions: all claim ops go through withArtifactWriteAuthority(repoPath, 'ISSUE-<hash>', op)
postconditions: LOCK ORDERING: claim mutex (key ISSUE-<hash>) is always acquired BEFORE any artifact write on ISSUE-<hash>, EPIC-<hash>, STORY-<hash>-s1, PENDING-CREATE file; nested artifact writes inside a claim op run under the same authority so ordering is consistent (claim lock -> artifact write). Never the reverse: an artifact write in progress never blocks claim acquisition for longer than the current op because the claim key is distinct from the artifact key.
Cross-process correctness comes from the lock-directory guard (dead-owner quarantine); the authority queue serializes in-process work on the same key.
Test crosses the REAL worker/authority boundary: a daemon worker calls the authority handler with key ISSUE-<hash> and the claim op runs inside it (not a local mutex mock).

migrationSteps.action: No migration/backfill: in-process behavior fix. stateBefore: tracker stages throw at context read (requireApprovedEpic DEF-only) and ENOENT at finalize persistence (mutateEpicTrackerMeta/sync.ts DEF json) for ISSUE-headed items; chain reports chain-complete for unpushed ISSUE items; the approval-created issueRef is invisible to push; linkDocsToIssues would duplicate docs under docs/epics. stateAfter: all five layers kind-aware; existing ISSUE-anchored items adopt their approval-created ref automatically on the next tracker run (existingRefs seeded from ISSUE.meta.tracker.issueRef). No stored data rewritten.

migration.stateAfter: tracker.push/sync/post accept, persist and link ISSUE-anchored work items end to end: meta.tracker lands on ISSUE-<hash>.json with EPIC/STORY-s1 unit bindings (zero DEF files fabricated); the chain offers push-tracker -> sync-tracker -> chain-complete for approved ISSUE items; the approval-created GitHub issue is adopted with zero duplicate creates and conflict refusal; docs relink under docs/standalone with ISSUE.md refreshed and no docs/epics duplicate.
migration.stateBefore: Every tracker layer was DEF-only: context assemblers via requireApprovedEpic, persistence via DEF json paths in mutateEpicTrackerMeta (orchestrator.ts:2972) and sync.ts:59/106, storiesOf via readDefineArtifact (sync.ts:164); chain computeNextAction ISSUE branch skipped tracker steps (chain.ts:325-360); unitIssueOf reads only EPIC/STORY head bindings so ISSUE.meta.tracker.issueRef was invisible; linkDocsToIssues hardcoded 'epic' placement (link.ts:46-57).

summary.prose: Final LLD (closing the rev-3 review's 1 HIGH + 2 MED on top of the pass-3 five-layer design): tracker.push/sync/post fully support ISSUE-anchored work items. (HIGH) Context schemas gain optional headKind; pushPrompt/pushVerifyPrompt (src/workflow/runners/tracker/index.ts) emit an ISSUE block for headKind 'issue' — ONE issue, the prerendered ISSUE markdown as the single authoritative body, labels epicLabel + epic:<slug> only, no task-list/back-reference/sub-issues (self-references), and adoption of an existing epicRef WITHOUT --force (the 'existingRefs error unless --force' rule does not apply to adopted ISSUE refs); the ISSUE verify checklist is issueLabelled + bodyMatches + singleIssue. Prompt-text unit tests pin both kinds; DEF is byte-identical at code and prompt level. (MED) One readable-head rule — readArtifactCore first-READABLE-wins, DEF then ISSUE, same as storage.ts readEpicDefinitionCore — backs requireApprovedDefinition, definitionHeadJsonPath and every persistence site (mutateEpicTrackerMeta, sync.ts), so a corrupt DEF can never be persisted into while context reads the ISSUE; corrupt-DEF/valid-ISSUE finalize test proves it. (MED) First publication with no issueRef (approved while tracking disabled): the ISSUE prompt creates exactly ONE remote issue, finalize writes the ref back to ISSUE.meta.tracker.issueRef AND binds EPIC/STORY-s1 heads so closeBugfixTrackerIssue can close at completion; a partial run adopts on retry with zero duplicate creates. Pass-3 layers unchanged: persistence via the resolved head, chain ISSUE branch (push-tracker -> sync-tracker -> chain-complete, no HLD/amendment/stale), adoption of ISSUE.meta.tracker.issueRef as the single root+s1 issue, kind-aware linkDocsToIssues placement under docs/standalone.
